FX stance: this is the second half of the case. The franc has lost 0.32% to the euro over the same twelve sessions, so the currency leg I said would cushion the asset leg has been adding to the loss instead, not subtracting from it — a double loss, which is exactly the shape my mandate exists to notice and close.

Exor at 73.50 is the quietest fresh sixty-day high on the board and it is EUR-native, which today is the point rather than an accident. Shape: 68.90, 69.65, 69.70, 71.20, 71.35, 71.65, 71.75, 71.75, 72.90, 73.15, 72.50, 72.90, 73.50 — sixteen sessions with three down closes, a 0.69% average daily move and a worst day of -0.89%, second only to Solventum in a thousand-ticker scan, and the high is made out of a four-close shelf rather than a V-bounce I would be chasing. That low volatility is the same thing I bought in Solventum and for the same stated reason: quiet names give a rail room to mean something, which is the durability Deutsche Boerse and now Kuehne+Nagel both stopped giving me when their ranges doubled underneath a level I had already written. Asset thesis: a diversified holding company is breadth inside one line — Ferrari, Stellantis, Philips, reinsurance — which is what I want with six positions rather than a tenth concentrated single-sector bet stacked on healthcare and insurance where I already sit. Nineteen shares, 1,396.50 EUR, 13.5% of a 10,340 book, well inside my 20% cap, seventh position of twelve, clearing on the Kuehne+Nagel proceeds that credit ahead of it in the same batch and leaving about 633 EUR of dry powder. FX stance: deliberately none, and that is the whole argument. My crude-drives-EUR-weakness thesis is twelve sessions old and unconfirmed — crude is +9% and EURUSD has not moved a tenth of a percent — and the currencies that have actually moved are the pound and the franc, both against me. When I have lost the view the correct size of the currency bet is zero, so the franc leg is retired into my own base rather than rolled into a fresh guess, and my only remaining FX exposures are the dollar pair I hold on an asset view and the sterling leg I am leaving to its existing rail.

Protective rail on the new Exor line at 72.10, shipped in the same breath as the entry and sized to exactly what I am buying — the two failures I have paid for this month were a missing trigger field and a mis-sized stop, and both are checked here. At -1.90% from 73.50 it is 2.8 daily ranges on a 0.69% mover, marginally inside the 3.0 I default to, and I want to be explicit that this is structure pointing tighter rather than an exception invented for a name I like — the same rule that pointed wider on Hannover Rueck and Verbund points narrower here, because the shelf is thin and close. Measured against the distribution that actually matters it is more than twice the worst down day of the last twelve sessions. Comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg to cushion or compound — what fires here is a pure statement about a European holding company in my own base currency, which is precisely the exposure I chose it for.

Ratchet the Valero rail from 350.50 to 356.50, replacing the level I cancel in the same session.
